cards.explanation: The answer is that they refuse to welcome Him. Luke says the people there refused to welcome Him, because He was heading for Jerusalem. The advance team went in and the village said no. That's a closed door, friends.

The answer is fire. James and John, two of Jesus' disciples, ask, “Lord, do You want us to call down fire from heaven to consume them?” That's a heavy question, friends. They brought it straight to Jesus and asked Him.
The answer is True. Luke 9:55 says, “But Jesus turned and rebuked them.” That's all the verse tells us about how He answers, friends. He turns, He rebukes, and then the story moves on.

The answer is False. Luke says, “And He and His disciples went on to another village.” They don't stay in the Samaritan village. They head on to the next one, and I bet there were a lot of questions on that walk.

The answer is that He has no place to lay His head. Jesus says, “Foxes have dens and birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.” Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10). Even a fox gets a den, and the One who made the foxes has no place to lay His head. The man had said he'd follow wherever Jesus goes, and this is what that road looks like.

The answer is to proclaim the kingdom of God. Jesus tells the man, “You, however, go and proclaim the kingdom of God.” That's the job He hands this man, friends. Luke doesn't tell us what the man does next.

The answer is True. Still another man says, “I will follow You, Lord; but first let me bid farewell to my family.” He's the third person on the road with something to say to Jesus, friends. And Jesus gives him an answer, which comes next in verse 62.

The answer is that he looks back. Jesus says, “No one who puts his hand to the plow and then looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.” The picture is a man with his hand on the plow who looks back. It's like trying to walk a straight line while staring over your shoulder, friends. You're not going where you're pointed.
